summary: Indexed text lookup over a linked list of UI items. this+0x90 holds the list head and this+0x94 holds the item count; when index a2 is in [0, count), walks the head node forward a2 steps via the next-node pointer at +0x8C and returns the string pointer at +0xA0. Returns byte_5EA438 as the default when the index is out of range, a node is missing mid-walk, or the target string is null. Called by sub_46BA20 (0046BA20).

local_names.a2: zero-based item index to look up
local_names.v3: current node pointer during the linked-list walk
local_names.v4: walk iteration counter compared against a2

operations.description: Bounds check: return the byte_5EA438 default unless a2 is in [0, this+0x94) where this+0x94 is the item count
Head check: seed the walk from v3 = this+0x90 (list head, this[36]); when it is null, fall through and return the default
Iteration: while v4 < a2, advance v3 to *(v3 + 0x8C) (next-node link) and increment v4; if v3 becomes null mid-walk, return the byte_5EA438 default
Read result = *(v3 + 0xA0) (string text field of the reached node); when result is null return the byte_5EA438 default instead
Return the resolved string pointer, or byte_5EA438 when the index was out of range or any step of the lookup failed
Consumed by sub_46BA20 (0046BA20) to fetch the text of the item at a given index

unresolved: The deterministic field facts address the node's next-pointer and string fields through base *(this+0x11C) while the raw decompiled body seeds the walk from this[36] (+0x90); whether those two addressing forms denote the same list storage is not proven here
